person.name: Patrick Manswell
person.headline: Computer science student at Trinity College (May 2027) building Java web services and AI integrations.
person.looking_for: Software engineering roles on the East Coast where I can apply my skills in AI, testing, and web services.

projects.name: FHIR Lite Patient Explorer
projects.my_role: Solo: built the Spring Boot backend, the PostgreSQL schema and seed data, the Docker Compose setup, and the React/TypeScript UI.
projects.evidence: Public repo: REST controllers for Patient, Encounter, Medication, Observation and CareGap with MRN search, Swagger UI, seeded synthetic patients, Docker Compose for backend + database. No automated tests.

annotation.what_is_this: A personal project I built to learn Java, Spring Boot, and PostgreSQL.
annotation.why_this_choice: A professor recommended this stack to me. I also felt most comfortable in Java, since all of my introductory CS courses were taught in it, so it was the language I knew best.
annotation.what_breaks: Looking at the repo now: it has no automated tests, so a change could break an endpoint without anyone noticing. The database password is a default value in the config files, which is fine for a local demo with synthetic patients but not for real patient data.
annotation.what_did_i_learn: I learned the core skills of backend development, along with agile development practices and version control with Git.

projects.name: EHR Reconciliation Engine
projects.my_role: Solo: take-home assessment for the EHR Integration Intern role at Onye. Built the Express server, the Claude prompts and structured-output handling, the React client, and the server tests.
projects.evidence: Live demo on Vercel; 9 Vitest server tests covering input validation, response shape, implausible vitals (BP 340/180 flagged high severity), request caching (Claude called once for identical payloads), and API-key middleware, with the Claude call mocked.

annotation.what_is_this: A take-home project I built as part of a job application. It reconciles a patient's medical data from different sources into a single report.
annotation.why_this_choice: I used TypeScript and Express because that was the stack suggested by the founder of Onye, the company I was applying to.
annotation.what_breaks: The confidence score comes entirely from Claude, so a wrong or overconfident reconciliation isn't caught by code. The response cache is an in-memory map that resets when the server restarts, there's no duplicate detection when two sources describe the same record, and the API is protected by a single shared key. My README lists these as what I'd improve with more time.
annotation.what_did_i_learn: This was my first experience calling an AI API from my own code.

projects.name: Cloud-Native Fitness Challenge Tracker
projects.my_role: From the git history (71 of 262 commits): the React frontend (fitness-app-react-ui), the auth-service (JWT and Spring Security) and user-service in Java Spring Boot, Kubernetes manifests, config maps and ingress for user, auth and frontend, GitHub Actions CI/CD for auth, user and frontend, AI coach prompt fixes (stricter JSON output, input sanitizing), and the user guide. Teammates built the leaderboard, challenge and workout services and most of the original screens.
projects.evidence: Team repo with 4 contributors; k8s/ manifests, .github/workflows/ CI per service, architecture and ER diagrams, user guide. Credit only what my_role lists.

annotation.what_is_this: A class project: a gamified fitness app where you can compete with friends and draft a workout routine based on your interests and goals.
annotation.why_this_choice: The course was built around learning cloud-native development, and the project called for many microservices. We hosted it on our professor's Kubernetes cluster in his homelab.
annotation.what_breaks: The deployment depended on pieces outside our code. We couldn't log in to Harbor to push our images, the ingress routing between the frontend and the backend services broke until we fixed the routes and the host name, and when a service like auth, challenge, or workout wasn't running, the UI couldn't reach it.
annotation.what_did_i_learn: I worked as part of a team, and this project was my introduction to cloud-native development and CI/CD.
